status: drafted directly per established methodology (single-pass, not the multi-agent OT workflow); adversarially fact-checked and corrected, pending user review
notes: Jude is the shortest and most urgent letter in the KJV New Testament (a single 25-verse chapter), built almost entirely around one collective antagonist (false teachers who have "crept in unawares") and a rapid volley of illustrative allusions rather than an on-page narrative -- so the tier structure leans heavily law/theme-typed rather than person-typed: only Jude himself (the author, personally exhorting readers and closing the letter) and the collective false teachers (present-tense, currently active among the readers, vividly described but never individuated by name) get true person/manager tiers. Every OT or traditional example Jude cites -- the wilderness generation, the fallen angels, Sodom and Gomorrha, Cain, Balaam, Core, Michael's dispute with the devil over Moses's body, Enoch's prophecy, the apostles' earlier warning -- is grouped into five law-tiers by rhetorical function, each carrying a "deliveredBy" pointing to whichever voice Jude is actually quoting or narrating for that block: himself for the OT judgment precedents, the Michael/Moses episode, and the Cain/Balaam/Core list; Enoch for the directly-quoted prophecy; and the apostles collectively for their earlier warning about mockers. Individually-named figures inside those law tiers (Cain, Balaam, Core, Enoch, Michael the archangel, the devil) get lightweight "named" entries carrying only their Jude-specific verse plus any collision flags, since their full narratives already live in their home books (Genesis, Numbers). James -- named only for Jude's self-identification in v.1 and taking no action in the text -- likewise gets a standalone lightweight "named" entry rather than being bucketed with the truly anonymous collectives, for consistency with how Cain/Balaam/Core/Michael/the devil are each treated despite equally brief mentions; only the genuinely unnamed collectives (the Exodus generation, the fallen angels, Sodom and Gomorrha) remain in genealogyLists, per the rule against inventing individuation the text doesn't support. Two real scholarly-tradition flags are carried explicitly, per this book's own unusual features: Jude 1:9's dispute over the body of Moses draws on a tradition not found in the OT canon as preserved in the KJV (widely associated with the largely-lost Assumption/Testament of Moses), and Jude 1:14-15 directly quotes material paralleling the non-canonical Book of Enoch (1 Enoch 1:9) -- both described neutrally here, with no position taken on canonicity. Jude's own identity is flagged as a real naming-collision case, distinct from Judas Iscariot and from Judas/Thaddaeus the apostle (Matthew 10:3); his traditional identification as a half-brother of Jesus, via the "Judas" listed in Matthew 13:55/Mark 6:3, is marked explicitly as a traditional inference rather than something Jude's own opening verse states outright (it says only "brother of James"); the genealogy.father/mother fields for both Jude and James now use the project's standard concise "identification -- reference" string format instead of prose paragraphs, matching cain_jude/balaam_jude/etc. elsewhere in this file. Jude 1:17's third-person reference to "the apostles" is noted as a textual clue supporting the traditional view that Jude was not himself one of the twelve. Tier-type flag for the user to confirm: "law_michael_moses_body" (The Archangel's Rebuke) is kept as a law/theme tier for consistency with the book's other OT-allusion blocks, but Michael is narratively active in Jude 1:9 (he disputes, refrains from a railing accusation, and speaks a line) rather than merely transmitting teaching -- closer to the book's own "personally embodied" test (used to justify Jude and the false teachers getting person tiers) than to the "pure transmission" test used for the Enoch and apostles law tiers. Given the letter's extreme brevity and single-verse scope for this episode, it was left as a law tier rather than promoted to a full person/manager tier, but this is a judgment call, not a clean-cut application of the rule -- flagged here and again on the tier's own funFacts for visibility. Jude 1:10 ("these speak evil of those things which they know not...") was originally double-listed under both "ungodly_intruders" and "law_michael_moses_body"; resolved by keeping it solely under "ungodly_intruders" (its actual subject -- "these," the false teachers) and trimming "law_michael_moses_body" to its core content, Jude 1:8-9, since v.10 was a copy/paste bridging artifact rather than an intentional dual reference.

scribeTiers.scribeName: The Way of Cain, the Error of Balaam, the Gainsaying of Core
Enoch's Prophecy of the Ten Thousands

characters.name: Jude

genealogy.father: Unstated in Jude's own text (v.1 says only 'brother of James'); traditionally Joseph the carpenter -- cf. Matthew 13:55/Mark 6:3 (see funFacts)
genealogy.mother: Unstated in Jude's own text; traditionally Mary, mother of Jesus -- cf. Matthew 13:55/Mark 6:3 (see funFacts)

verses.note: Identifies himself as 'the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James,' addressing the letter to those 'sanctified by God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ, and called.'
Opens with a greeting: 'Mercy unto you, and peace, and love, be multiplied.'
Explains he meant to write of 'the common salvation' but felt compelled instead to exhort the readers to 'earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints.'
Tells readers to 'remember ye the words which were spoken before of the apostles' -- referring to the apostles in the third person.

Closing exhortation: build up on 'most holy faith,' pray in the Holy Ghost, keep in God's love, look for mercy unto eternal life; have compassion on some, and save others 'with fear, pulling them out of the fire,' while hating 'the garment spotted by the flesh.'
Closing doxology: 'unto him that is able to keep you from falling... to the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen.'

funFacts: Naming-collision flag: this Jude is distinct from Judas Iscariot (the betrayer) and from Judas/Thaddaeus/Lebbaeus, one of the twelve apostles (Matthew 10:3, Luke 6:16). Jude 1:17's third-person reference to 'the apostles' (rather than 'we apostles') textually distinguishes this Jude from that group, consistent with the traditional view that he is the Lord's brother rather than one of the twelve.

Traditionally identified with the 'Judas' listed among Jesus's brothers in Matthew 13:55 and Mark 6:3 -- but Jude's own text (v.1) states only 'brother of James,' without further identification; this project flags the identification as traditional, not textually certain within this epistle.

Also traditionally identified as the brother of the same James who authored the Epistle of James and is called 'the Lord's brother' in Galatians 1:19 -- again a traditional linkage between two brief self-identifications, not stated outright in either epistle.

characters.name: The Ungodly Intruders

verses.note: 'Certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ.'
'These filthy dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities.'
'These speak evil of those things which they know not: but what they know naturally, as brute beasts, in those things they corrupt themselves.'
'Spots in your feasts of charity... clouds they are without water, carried about of winds; trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots.'
'Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever.'
'Murmurers, complainers, walking after their own lusts; and their mouth speaketh great swelling words, having men's persons in admiration because of advantage.'
Identified as the 'mockers' foretold by the apostles, who 'walk after their own ungodly lusts... separate themselves, sensual, having not the Spirit.'

funFacts: Kept as a single collective entry rather than individuated persons -- the text never names or differentiates specific individuals within this group, describing them only through a rapid series of collective images (spots, clouds, trees, waves, stars).

Jude 1:10 is deliberately listed only here, not also under the 'law_michael_moses_body' tier -- 'these' in v.10 refers back to this group (the false teachers), continuing the contrast the law tier draws with Michael's restraint in vv.8-9, but the group itself is this entry's subject.

characters.name: OT Judgment Precedents
characters.purpose: Three precedents of certain judgment despite prior favor or status, used to warn that ancestry or spiritual privilege does not exempt anyone from judgment: the LORD's own delivered people perished in unbelief after the Exodus (v.5), the angels who abandoned their proper estate are held in chains awaiting judgment (v.6), and Sodom and Gomorrha suffer as a public example of eternal fire's vengeance (v.7) -- each escalating the case that the false teachers now among the readers face the same certain fate.

verses.note: 'The Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not.'
'The angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.'

'Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.'

characters.name: Michael and the Body of Moses
characters.purpose: Contrasts the false teachers' brazen 'railing accusation' against spiritual dignities with the restraint of Michael the archangel, who -- even disputing directly with the devil over the body of Moses -- did not presume to bring a railing accusation himself but deferred to the Lord ('The Lord rebuke thee'); illustrates that even the greatest of created beings shows more restraint than the men Jude condemns.

verses.note: 'Likewise also these filthy dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities.'
'Yet Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil he disputed about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, The Lord rebuke thee.'

funFacts: Verse 9 references a dispute over Moses's body that is not recorded anywhere in the Old Testament canon as preserved in the KJV; it is widely associated by scholars with a now-largely-lost Jewish work sometimes called the Assumption of Moses or Testament of Moses. This is flagged as Jude's use of an extra-biblical tradition, described here only as it appears in the KJV text itself, without asserting the lost work's contents as scripture.

Tier-type flag: Michael is narratively active here (disputes, restrains himself, speaks a line) rather than purely transmitting teaching, which sits closer to this book's 'personally embodied' test for a person/manager tier than to the 'pure transmission' test used for the Enoch and apostles law tiers. Kept as a law tier given the episode's single-verse scope and this letter's extreme brevity -- a judgment call flagged for the user to confirm, not a clean rule application.

characters.name: The Apostasy Examples
characters.scribeTier: The Way of Cain, the Error of Balaam, the Gainsaying of Core
characters.purpose: A pronounced 'Woe' listing three OT figures whose sins model three distinct failures Jude sees repeated in the false teachers: Cain's murderous hatred of a righteous brother, Balaam's greed that led him to sell his gift for reward, and Core's (Korah's) rebellion against divinely ordained authority -- three different roads to the same 'perishing.'

verses.note: 'Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.'

characters.name: Enoch's Prophecy
characters.scribeTier: Enoch's Prophecy of the Ten Thousands
characters.purpose: Jude directly quotes a prophecy attributed to Enoch, 'the seventh from Adam' (Genesis 5), foretelling the Lord's coming with 'ten thousands of his saints' to execute judgment and convict the ungodly of their deeds and hard speeches -- used as a final, ancient witness confirming certain judgment is coming for the very kind of men Jude has been describing throughout the letter.

verses.note: 'And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints.'

'To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.'

funFacts: This is the only place in the KJV New Testament that directly quotes material corresponding to a passage from the non-canonical Book of Enoch (paralleling 1 Enoch 1:9) as though it were an authoritative prophecy -- a genuinely unusual feature of this short epistle, noted here descriptively; this project takes no position on canonicity beyond describing what the KJV text itself does.

characters.name: The Apostles' Prophecy of Mockers
characters.purpose: Jude reminds his readers of a prediction already made by 'the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ' -- that mockers walking after their own ungodly lusts would arise in the last time -- and identifies the false teachers currently troubling the readers as the fulfillment of that very warning, men who 'separate themselves, sensual, having not the Spirit.'

verses.note: 'But, beloved, remember ye the words which were spoken before of the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ.'
'How that they told you there should be mockers in the last time, who should walk after their own ungodly lusts.'
'These be they who separate themselves, sensual, having not the Spirit.'

funFacts: Jude's third-person reference to 'the apostles' (rather than 'we apostles') is a textual clue supporting the traditional view that Jude himself was not one of the twelve -- see Jude's own character entry.

characters.name: Michael the Archangel

verses.note: Contends with the devil in a dispute over the body of Moses; refuses to bring a railing accusation, saying only 'The Lord rebuke thee.'

funFacts: Named elsewhere in scripture as 'the archangel' and 'one of the chief princes' (Daniel 10:13, 21; 12:1) and as the one who fights the dragon in Revelation 12:7 -- this entry covers only his appearance in Jude 1:9, not a full cross-book profile.

The dispute over Moses's body is not itself narrated in the OT text (Deuteronomy 34:5-6 says only that the LORD buried Moses 'in a valley... but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day') -- see the law tier's funFacts for the extra-biblical tradition this verse appears to draw on.

characters.name: The Devil

verses.note: Disputes with Michael the archangel over the body of Moses; Michael declines to rail against him directly.

funFacts: Called 'the devil' here without further identification. Scripture elsewhere applies the title 'that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan' (Revelation 12:9) to the tempter of Genesis 3, but that identification is made explicitly only in Revelation, not within Jude or Genesis themselves -- flagged rather than assumed.

characters.name: Cain

spouses: unnamed wife -- Genesis 4:17, not individually indexed here
children: Enoch (Cain's son -- Genesis 4:17; a different man from the Enoch quoted in Jude 1:14, see funFacts)

verses.note: Cited as the archetype of 'the way of' murderous hatred toward a righteous brother; full narrative indexed in Genesis.

funFacts: Naming-collision flag: not to be confused with Enoch 'the seventh from Adam' quoted three verses later in Jude 1:14 -- that Enoch descends through Seth's line (Genesis 5), while a different, unrelated man also named Enoch appears here as Cain's own son (Genesis 4:17).

verses.note: Cited as the archetype of 'the error of' greed -- running 'greedily after... reward'; full narrative indexed in Numbers.

characters.name: Core (Korah)

verses.note: Cited as the archetype of 'the gainsaying of' -- rebellion against Moses and Aaron's divinely ordained authority; full narrative (and his destruction) indexed in Numbers 16.

funFacts: 'Core' is the KJV's Greek-influenced transliteration of the Hebrew name rendered 'Korah' in the Old Testament (e.g. Numbers 16) -- same person, spelling difference only.

characters.name: Enoch

verses.note: Identified as 'the seventh from Adam' (counting Adam-Seth-Enos-Cainan-Mahalaleel-Jared-Enoch, per Genesis 5) and credited with prophesying the Lord's coming in judgment.
Content of the quoted prophecy: judgment upon the ungodly for their deeds and hard speeches against the Lord.

funFacts: Naming-collision flag: this is the Sethite Enoch of Genesis 5 (father of Methuselah, who 'walked with God: and he was not; for God took him,' Genesis 5:24) -- a different man from Cain's son Enoch in Genesis 4:17.

The quoted prophecy does not appear anywhere in the Old Testament text itself; it closely parallels a passage from the non-canonical Book of Enoch (1 Enoch 1:9), which Jude appears to quote directly -- see the law tier's funFacts for further detail.

characters.name: The Apostles

verses.note: Referenced collectively as having foretold that mockers walking after their own ungodly lusts would arise in the last time.

funFacts: Kept as a single collective reference per the rule against inventing individuation the text doesn't support -- Jude does not name or differentiate any specific apostle here, referring to them only as a group whose prior teaching he is reminding readers of.

characters.name: James

genealogy.father: Unstated in Jude's own text; traditionally Joseph the carpenter -- cf. Matthew 13:55/Mark 6:3 (see funFacts)
genealogy.mother: Unstated in Jude's own text; traditionally Mary, mother of Jesus -- cf. Matthew 13:55/Mark 6:3 (see funFacts)

verses.note: Named only for Jude's self-identification -- 'Jude... the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James.' James himself takes no action in this text.

funFacts: Given a standalone lightweight entry (rather than folded into genealogyLists) for consistency with how this file treats other single-mention named figures who take no action -- Cain, Balaam, Core, Michael the archangel, and the devil all get the same treatment despite equally brief citations.

Naming-collision flag: the KJV New Testament has multiple men named James -- James son of Zebedee (one of the twelve, Matthew 4:21), James son of Alphaeus (another of the twelve, Matthew 10:3), and this James. This entry makes no claim about which James Jude means beyond what Jude 1:1 itself states.

Traditionally identified with James the author of the Epistle of James, himself traditionally called 'the Lord's brother' (Galatians 1:19), and traditionally with the 'James' listed among Jesus's brothers in Matthew 13:55/Mark 6:3 -- both are traditional linkages, not stated outright in Jude's own text.

genealogyLists.note: Bulk or deliberately-unresolved references, kept out of the character list above -- reserved for genuinely unnamed/anonymous collectives only (named single-mention figures, including James, now get their own lightweight character entries above for consistency).

israel_wilderness_generation.note: 'The people' the Lord saved out of Egypt and later destroyed for unbelief -- a collective reference to the Exodus generation, not individuated by name in Jude; full narrative indexed under Exodus/Numbers.

fallen_angels.note: 'The angels which kept not their first estate' -- an unnamed collective, reserved in chains under darkness until judgment; not individuated by name.

sodom_and_gomorrha.note: Cited as a public example of judgment by 'eternal fire' for sexual sin -- collective city-names, not individuated by name; full narrative indexed under Genesis 19.
